St Helen and St Katharine is a school where bright girls with enquiring minds thrive, as they grow into intellectually curious and erudite young women. Academic life is full, vibrant and spirited: the best within and beyond the classroom combine to stimulate intellectual endeavour and inquisitive independence which embody the ethos of our school.
A sense of purposeful fun
We take having fun very seriously and ensure students have the opportunity to take a break. Dressing up days or simply a hot chocolate around the campfire give students the chance to go off-curriculum and take part in activities which are different from their academic studies. This is just as much a part of a fully-rounded education as what happens in the classroom.
Sarah Rollings, Head

Computer Science
There are few aspects of our world that are not facilitated, monitored or controlled by computers. Computers were designed to make our lives easier; to make calculations quicker and more accurate, to help break codes, and to assist scientists and mathematicians in finding life-changing solutions to complex problems. In addition to understanding how computers work, students will develop analytical problem-solving and computational thinking skills that have applications across all subjects and walks of life. Students will learn resilience and tenacity as they become independent problem solvers who are comfortable making mistakes and willing to sometimes start again.
The subject is supported by two computing suites and a range of digital and physical resources that students are encouraged to explore and make use of across all curricular and extracurricular areas.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
The Computer Science curriculum builds foundations and confidence in digital literacy. SHSK Prep students learn how systems and networks work, how to deal with data and information, and how to create digital media, building their programming skills in a range of contexts. This includes projects on creating podcasts, building their own computer games and designing a smart school. Online safety is woven throughout the Computer Science curriculum, supporting students to develop the skills and awareness needed to keep themselves safe in an increasingly digital world when working, socialising or having fun online.
Lower School
In Year 7, students start by building strong foundations for programming and computational thinking skills by creating the game Pacman in Scratch – a block-based programming language that allows students to learn programming constructs without getting caught up in simple spelling mistakes. Students will then create sound effects to use within their game, learning the difference between analogue and digital sound and how it is represented on a computer. The year finishes with students designing a logo for their Pacman game using the vector-based drawing software Adobe Illustrator. Students will look at the differences between bitmap and vector graphics and employ an iterative analysis and design process to create effective logos using complex shapes.
In Year 8, students focus on more advanced programming skills, making the transition from Scratch to Python by completing several programming projects, including a school report generator and games of chance. Students build on their algorithm design skills learnt in Year 7 by creating more complex flowcharts and using pseudocode and will make use of functions to produce programs that are efficient and easily maintainable. Students will also investigate past, present and future computing technologies, as well as learn how to give an effective presentation using the digital resources available.
Middle School
Students start Year 9 by investigating binary – how it works, how to convert between number systems, and designing and creating a program to perform that conversion. Students learn that everything a computer deals with is represented as binary – including characters, images and logic. Next, students design and create a text-based adventure game using functions to produce an ever-expandable game where players make decisions in order to survive the perils thrown at them.
In their final term, students answer the question ‘How does the web work?’ as they look at the difference between the ‘internet’ and the ‘world wide web’, as well as the techniques unscrupulous web developers use to trick users into giving up personal data. Students then design their own website using HTML and CSS following best practices and considering the needs of all users.
Students can choose to take GCSE Computer Science as one of their GCSE options. In the first year of the course, the focus is on algorithm design, programming constructs and programming skills with a mix of short tasks and more complex programming challenges. Students also look at the representation of data in computer systems and computer components.
In the second year of their GCSE course, students gain a theoretical understanding of networking in both design and defence and consider the ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impact of digital technologies with topics such as artificial intelligence (AI), social media and legislation.
Sixth Form
Students have the opportunity to study A level Computer Science in the Sixth Form. This two-year course builds on the topics studied in GCSE Computer Science and adds complexity, depth and additional topics, such as database design and web technologies.
The A level also includes a substantial programming project on an area of the student’s choice. Past projects have included physics modelling and AI handwriting recognition using neural networks.

Academic enrichment
In class, students take part in the Bebras Computing Challenge in November to further develop computational thinking skills, with our most gifted students from Years 10 upwards completing the British Informatics Olympiad in December. Mixed groups of Year 9, 10 and 11 students are able to enter the Perse Challenge, a team-based coding challenge designed to test problem-solving skills in a collaborative environment.
Extracurricular
Our TechSpace club provides an opportunity for students to tackle their own computing-related projects independently, making use of the equipment and software available in the computing rooms. Students can take up physical computing projects using micro:bits, Arduinos and a range of Kitrontic Robotics. Students can learn to build their own PC, with a lunchtime club focused on hardware or explore the virtual world at the afterschool VR club. Students might also choose to develop their digital creative design skills with Blender, GameMaker and Adobe Creative Suite.

French
Bonjour! Learning French at St Helen and St Katharine is a fun and rewarding experience, offering students numerous benefits for academic and future career prospects.
Indeed, it can open up a world of opportunities. With over 275 million speakers worldwide, French is an official language of the United Nations, the European Union, UNESCO and the International Red Cross. As a GCSE and A level student, proficiency in French can lead to exciting possibilities such as studying abroad, working internationally and engaging with different cultures.
Learning French can boost your cognitive skills and academic performance. Research shows that learning a new language can improve brain function and boost memory, concentration and critical thinking skills. Studies have also shown that students who study French tend to perform better in standardised tests and that they are linguistically more equipped to absorb new languages in the future.
Activities in French classes are varied, and we also enhance students’ learning experience by offering interactive learning activities on a range of platforms – such as Active Hub, Languagegym, Linguascope and more – as well as giving access to authentic resources, eg magazines, podcasts, news outlets and songs.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
Learning a language is a great opportunity to explore a different culture. This is done through dedicated language learning lessons as well as celebration of different cultural festivals.
Our primary language in SHSK Prep is French. As students progress through Years 3 to 6 the amount of curriculum time increases, as does the complexity. Focus, at this age, is on learning basic structures and phrases, as well as fostering a ‘have a go’ attitude.
Lower School
Learning a new language can be challenging but also exciting. French is a popular language in Year 8 with between two and three groups of 20 students opting for it at the end of Year 7.
The course starts at a beginner level to ensure all participating have a solid command of the basics. Students who have studied French before not only enjoy consolidating their knowledge but also expand it through stretching activities. Moreover, the fast rate of progress keeps all motivated.
Teachers use a variety of engaging resources alongside our main textbook, Dynamo 1. We incorporate multimedia tasks such as videos and audio to assist our students in their comprehension skills and our activities are designed to develop sound pronunciation, grammar and vocabulary in fun and interactive ways to achieve a high standard of accuracy.
Middle School
In Year 9, we continue to incorporate interesting topics such as music tastes, future plans, inventors, sports, friendship, as well as engaging current affairs topics such as the refugee crisis and environmental issues. This allows students to enhance their cultural knowledge and broaden their perspectives as well as advance their vocabulary and grammar.
By the end of Year 9, students are well equipped to start the GCSE course. We aim to build good learning habits, so pupils grow into self-motivated and resilient learner who have an open-mind and a genuine interest in French and the francophone cultures.
In Year 10 and 11, we usually have two groups of 15–24 students taking the AQA French GCSE. The course covers a wide range of topics aimed at developing students’ competence in the language. It is divided into three themes: People and lifestyle, Popular culture, and Communication and the world around us. Sub-topics include family and relationships, social media, music, French festivals, healthy eating and leisure activities such as sports, television and film.
Our teachers use a variety of resources that motivate students and help them to develop key language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking, as well as increasing their knowledge of French culture.
At the end of Year 10, and all through Year 11, French students have a timetable session with our French assistant. This is an invaluable opportunity that enhances their spoken fluency and also benefits their listening and writing skills.
Sixth Form
Studying A level French enables students to become near-fluent speakers on a plethora of topics, as well as enriches their personal growth and cultural awareness. French culture is known for its art, fashion, music, food and literature, and our curriculum is built to enable students to appreciate and understand these aspects even better.
Learning French at A level is an enjoyable yet challenging experience, but also an investment in the future. Speaking French can enable new connections with French-speaking people and communities, as well as the opportunity to forge new friendships and appreciate different perspectives. Additionally, bilingual French and English speakers are highly sought after in multilingual organisations, making proficiency in French a valuable asset for your future employment.

Academic enrichment
We always look for opportunities to add to the experience of our students and support their learning. For example, Year 9 take part in an MFL marketing day where they design and market a product to a target country. We also try to attend plays in French by the Onatti Theatre troupe as it is a great way of developing their listening skills and enthusing them about how much they understand already.
In the past, Year 11 and Sixth Form students have been invited to cinema evenings to discover more about French society and culture through the medium of film. Students have also attended webinars and a conference in London at the British Film Institute to look into French New Wave film directors.
In Year 10 and Year 11, students can sign up for our popular trip to Lyon. This trip includes French lessons in the morning and cultural excursions in the afternoon. In the evening, students stay in groups of two to three in host families where they get to practise their French and discover what daily life is in a French home.
A level students can go on our Joint Art, History and French long weekend in Paris. We spend four days exploring Paris, its museums, galleries, sights and cafés. A great opportunity to use their French and find out more about their course topics in situ.
Extracurricular
We run a lunchtime MFL Club for students, providing cultural sessions run by an MFL teacher and a group of Sixth Form students. Discussions have included French music, looking at French short stories and fairy tales, as well as making French food.

Drama
The Drama Department is a hub of creative activity at St Helen and St Katharine and Drama is a thriving part of school life both within and outside the classroom.
We offer a diverse range of theatrical opportunities beyond the curriculum and enjoy a reputation for creating dynamic, high-quality productions. Outside of the classroom, students perform in productions including a range of genres, styles and periods and participate in a wide variety of roles as actors, writers, designers, technicians and directors.
Curriculum Drama is taught throughout the school, with a strong uptake at both GCSE and A level. The Drama Department is staffed by specialist teachers who enjoy fostering students’ skills in theatre and performance. Drama studies are supported by our professionally trained Theatre technician and Drama assistant, who contribute to the specialist teaching of theatre design elements. Students are supported to develop independence and a high level of ability, often producing outstanding performance work and showcasing the talents of students both onstage and behind the scenes. Students develop their learning within our dedicated performance spaces, with lessons taking place in our Studio Theatre, Yolande Paterson Hall and Performing Arts Studio.
Within the classroom, students learn confidence and collaboration whilst their intellectual ability to analyse and evaluate different theatre techniques and practitioners is developed. This is complemented by a focus throughout the curriculum on building practical performance skills and understanding the importance of theatre as a means of exploring challenging issues. Through studying Drama, students develop a range of transferable skills, including teamwork, debating skills, creative problem solving and leadership students go on to apply these in a wide range of applications. We aim to foster an atmosphere of challenge and fun, above all developing students’ abilities as strong and articulate communicators.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
The main purpose of Drama lessons in SHSK Prep is to build confidence and enjoyment in creating and performing. There is a focus on developing the skills of working with others in groups, alongside fostering confident oracy skills. Each year begins with a skills-based unit enhancing their knowledge of drama techniques and vocabulary.
For Years 3 and 4, the focus of the first term will be the end-of-term Christmas celebration. Girls in Year 5 progress to a ‘play in a week’ and Year 6 will take the lead in the annual summer musical production. Parents are warmly invited to all of these events.
Lower School
Drama is taught as a practical subject in Lower School, and in Year 7 weekly double lessons offer students the opportunity to work together and build their confidence. Students learn how to interpret and perform a script and create their own performance projects, exploring contemporary script, physical theatre and Greek Myths. Throughout the year, emphasis is placed on collaboration and teamwork, fostering a ‘have a go’ attitude and inspiring every student to feel confident in presenting work to the class. We foster creativity and imagination through frequent games and improvisation exercises and encourage strong communication skills through negotiation and group work.
In Year 8, Drama maintains its practical focus, challenging students to step out of their comfort zone and encouraging them to use their ‘have a go’ attitude. Working in small groups, students are introduced to theatre practitioners and apply a range of practical performance skills, creating projects which enable them to put their learning into practice. They then learn to analyse and evaluate from an audience perspective, developing intellectual engagement. Drama is a fun and engaging subject, where each student is encouraged to build their confidence and to challenge themselves.
Middle School
In Year 9, Drama becomes an elective subject which is taught in one double lesson per week. It is a popular choice, with roughly two-thirds of the year group choosing to study the subject. Lessons retain their practical focus, and students are challenged to engage with new and more complex ideas as the year progresses. Students are guided by their teacher to direct and devise their own performances, exploring high impact acting enhanced by sound and lighting techniques. They learn how to create recorded media and use their skills to write, direct, perform and edit short films and radio plays. This Year 9 Drama culminates in a scripted performance project which develops their students’ ability to work independently and completes their preparations for GCSEs.
In Years 10 and 11, students use performance skills to create powerful and thought-provoking theatre. The GCSE course is taught in two double lessons per week, and study is balanced between practical and written work, enabling students to develop essay writing skills alongside practical performance ability. Students are encouraged to take a 360-degree view of theatre, learning about lighting, sound, set and costume and applying these performance to bring their own productions to life. Theatre trips to study professional productions help develop analytical and evaluative abilities and students develop a high level of academic fluency.
Working both independently and in small groups, students are inspired to create bold theatre to a high standard. Studying GCSE Drama equips students with a high level of academic rigour and analytical engagement. This varied subject instils confidence, teamwork and communication skills, which prepares students for A Level and beyond.
Sixth Form
Drama and Theatre in the Sixth Form opens up a new range of experiences and possibilities, with two double lessons being taught each week. At A level, students are invited to be academically curious, considering the role of theatre in modern society and becoming highly skilled at constructing convincing written and verbal arguments. Through studying contemporary and classical scripts and developing strong written analytical skills, students will take their understanding of acting and technical theatre design to the next level.
Detailed study of professional theatre companies and practitioners, such as Kneehigh and Punchdrunk, offers inspiration, which students then explore further through their own practical work. Performances take place in the Studio Theatre, our dedicated performance space. Visits from professional theatre companies introduce students to new techniques and trips to watch inspiring professional theatre productions provide students with the knowledge to create their own outstanding practical work.
Drama in the Sixth Form is an exciting opportunity to develop practical skills, academic depth and rigour, and to hone communication and leadership skills, whilst building a detailed knowledge of the creative world of drama and theatre. This equips students with a wealth of transferable skills, preparing them for further study in a broad range of subjects from Liberal Arts to Medicine and Law. Each year a number of students go on to study Drama either as a University subject, or to follow a professional training route at one of the UK’s prestigious Drama Schools.

Academic enrichment
The study of drama within lessons is supported by regular opportunities to watch dynamic and exciting professional productions outside of school. With regular trips to watch productions at the Oxford Playhouse, London Theatres, Bristol Old Vic and the Watermill Theatre in Newbury, students enjoy watching a wide range of theatre. Live Theatre forms a key part of the GCSE and A level courses and students review the productions they have watched, learning about both performance and theatre design elements. We also enjoy welcoming professional touring theatre companies to perform within our Studio Theatre at St Helen’s.
Recent theatre trips have included: My Neighbour Totoro, Warhorse, Witness for the Prosecution, The Other Place, The Party Girls, Piaf, Wonderboy, The Father and the Assassin, The Empress, The Crucible, The Boy With Two Hearts, Brief Encounter, Wuthering Heights, The Ocean at the End of the Lane, Six, An Inspector Calls, Broke, The Life of Pi.
In addition to theatre trips, students have the opportunity to watch a large catalogue of theatre productions online, along with reading a wide range of play texts to further their learning. Our academic curriculum is enhanced by workshops led by visiting theatre companies and industry professionals. Most recently, Year 9 students enjoyed a physical theatre workshop learning the techniques of Frantic Assembly, GCSE students undertook a devising workshop with The Paper Birds theatre company and A Level student worked with a visiting professional theatre designer, learning costume and set design.. The study of the core set text at GCSE is enriched by a biennial trip to Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre in London where students are able to tread the boards of the theatre themselves before watching a recording of the original production and exploring the original costume, set and lighting designs.
Students enjoy a wide range of enrichment experiences that vary each academic year and are always designed to enhance student learning. Offering access to the inspiring work of professional theatre makers gives our students the opportunity to apply their enhanced learning to their own work, inspiring them to achieve their very best both within and outside the classroom.
Co-curricular
Co-curricular Drama is a thriving part of school life. The Drama Department offers a diverse range of theatrical opportunities beyond the curriculum and enjoys a reputation for creating sophisticated and dynamic productions. Students enjoy developing their skills, getting to know new people and gaining a sense of accomplishment at being part of a large-scale creative project. We aim to provide a broad range of productions each year, with opportunities for every year group and many productions having a cast size of over 45 students. All of our productions are supported by student-led backstage teams, who take on a range of roles from stage manager to assistant director, all adding to the exciting creative buzz.
The annual Playwriting Competition is a key event for Years 7–9, offering students the opportunity to enter their own original scripts for performance. Drama scholars write, direct and perform in small productions involving students across the school. 125 Bursary Appeal
Throughout the history of St Helen and St Katharine, students have been able to come to our school because their families received assistance towards the fees.
We know that bursaries increase social mobility, inclusion and diversity and a more inclusive, diverse student body is beneficial for all students, broadening outlooks and better preparing them for life beyond St Helen’s.
As we approach our 125th anniversary, we wish to confirm our commitment to our charitable origins by increasing our bursary provision, funding more full bursaries and more Sixth Form bursaries to support the education of brilliant young women.
We are asking each member of the school community – alumnae, current and former parents – to support our bursary fund with a gift of £125, either as a one-off or by pledging just £25 a year for five years.
The world is ever-changing, and we must respond while remaining true to our core value of providing the best specialist education to girls and young women, whatever their financial circumstances.
Learn more about the appeal:
125 Bursary Appeal Donate now
Inspiring stories
If you want to know why we’re so passionate about supporting bursaries then please read these inspiring stories from our former students; each story is different, but each highlights the profound impact of a fee-assisted place at St Helen’s.
“When I received a bursary, the overriding feeling was one of hope. I was so excited to come to a school where the girls were so eager to learn and the only thing stopping you from doing well is you.
When I left St Helen’s one of my teachers recounted that when I first came here a lot of the staff used to call me Zebedee because I was just so excited to be here and I was kind of in awe of the fact that I was finally somewhere like this. I definitely do have the mentality – and I think St Helen’s instilled this in me – that if something crops up in life, I very much have the self-confidence that I will figure it out like I always do.
And I would not have the career that I have in immunology without St Helen’s. The simplest way to describe what I now do is, we receive cells from cancer patients, we genetically modify them, and then they’re infused back in to attack their cancer. It’s a very humbling experience, but I love it. I think ‘this is their chance, and I was involved in that and it’s amazing.’”
“I’ll never forget the day that the letter arrived, and I opened it in the bathroom while my mum looked on expectantly. It was a relief to everyone that I had got in. My ability had been recognised, and I was not being excluded on the basis of a lack of family finances; I was wanted by the school.
My time at St Helen’s was amazing. It was a puzzle to my teachers that I wanted to study Chemistry, Biology and English A level; but I knew where I was heading, and I knew I needed that English A level to keep the artist inside me happy. I applied to the three Osteopathic Colleges in the UK and still remember the day that I rang the two colleges that I did not wish to attend from the payphone up by the Chemistry labs.
I qualified as an Osteopath four years later and last year celebrated 25 years in practice. I play clarinet, saxophone and trombone in the local Big Band and have two stunning children. And it all started with that letter in the bathroom….”
“The bursary that enabled me to study at St Helen’s has shaped my life in many ways. I enjoyed my time at school, both being pushed academically and taking advantage of all the extra-curricular opportunities.
The support from the school, encouraging us to participate in various Olympiads and academic competitions, and especially throughout sixth form and the university admissions process, gave me the opportunity to study Natural Sciences at the University of Cambridge. I think this has been the single biggest influence on my career so far, opening many doors.
I am currently studying for a PhD in Biotechnology. I think my choice to continue as a woman in STEM is certainly impacted by my school life. Throughout my education, I never considered there to be barriers to any field and just followed what interested me the most.
I hope many more girls will grow up believing this, too.”
“I grew up in a family of very intellectually bright people who had little grasp of emotional intelligence – and even less of how to manage money! So, there was never any assumption that a paid-for education was an option. Luckily, I had the kind of brain that allowed me to get a scholarship, and I felt proud and pleased that I had got into this good school.
I fitted in like a hand into a glove. I loved the intellectual stimulation of all those different subjects, and the chance to talk about work and fun with equally interesting and curious young people. I simply would not have had the chance to get this sort of education anywhere else, and the preparation I received, as well as the opportunity to go to Cambridge where my father and grandfather had been before me, was much appreciated. I suspect that I would have been confident wherever I went, but St Helen’s gave me an outrageously enormous extra boost, that’s for sure.
As a result of this solid and inspiring foundation, I left Cambridge speaking 5 languages fluently, and an international career on the horizon. I now speak 8 languages, have lived and worked in 17 countries on 4 continents, and benefit from a rich and expansive world view, as well as friends and clients from the world over.”
“St Helen’s was and is a level playing field when it comes to everything that matters. Perhaps it is the close-knit community, or the supportive staff, or the life-long friendships. Regardless, I will forever be grateful to the Bursary for giving me the life-changing gift of becoming a St Helen’s girl.
There is no question that without the Bursary I wouldn’t have been able to experience the wealth of opportunities that I did. From travelling to Japan for a drama trip and to Germany for music tour, to representing the UK at the European Youth Parliament and representing the school as a prefect, I look back on every experience at St Helen’s with fondness.
For me, being in an environment where it was cool to be curious, where it wasn’t unusual to love learning and where it was OK to be unashamedly enthusiastic, has led me to where I am today. Now, I’m a ‘QI Elf’, working as a writer and researcher for the BBC Two television series QI.”
“I think one of the main benefits of attending St Helen’s was the fact that we had access to such great facilities: the library, the science labs, the art rooms, the language centre. I know that I wouldn’t have received such a fantastic education in the sciences, for example, in another school.
St Helen’s definitely instilled in me a passion for languages. I was offered a teaching job in Spain in 2015, and I jumped at the opportunity and have never looked back. St Helen’s set me up for this and my life would have been completely different if I had gone somewhere else. I will forever be grateful for the education I received, and I hope many more young women can benefit from the wide range of opportunities offered.”
“Thank you for my Bursary and Assisted Place, which kept me boarding at St Helen’s when my (grand)father was forced to take early retirement. Whilst he tried to warn me I might have to leave, both in my third year and when 6th Form approached, I knew St Helen’s was where I was meant to be.
I would never have been able to have taken Latin, Greek and Music A Levels at my local school, and would not have gone on to a Choral Scholarship at Oxford.
Thank you for making me me!”
“The St Helen’s exam was the first I had ever taken, and I was looking forward to it as it was rumoured we could have crisps at the break! Afterwards I was disappointed as I had forgotten the word thermometer which was the answer to one of the questions. I had no idea of the life changing nature of the day.
I was naughty, never deliberately, and the school patiently guided me for eight years. The education I received enabled me to go on to the University of Edinburgh, where I graduated with honours in Italian and French.
My working career has been huge fun. After graduating I received an offer from an upmarket tour operator which included France and Italy in its destinations. I arranged many holidays for clients, including one where the two mothers booked into the same hotel as the honeymoon couple, ‘to give them a nice surprise at breakfast’!
During lockdown I did a teaching degree and, with nice circularity, now teach pupils in receipt of bursaries. As you will guess, I have a real heart for the naughty ones! So, thank you, St Helen’s, for opening doors for me to higher education and beyond. I assure you it’s not just a school for perfect pupils: naughty ones thrive there too!”
Catherine, 1983 leaver
“I won a scholarship to attend St Helens in 1964. I was so lucky and grateful as my parents would never have been able to afford the fees. I really enjoyed my schooling and made many friends and still keep in touch.
I was so fortunate to learn to play the piano there and started in my first term and reached grade 6 when I left school. We were also encouraged to try other instruments which I did. Violin for a term (our dog used to howl when I tried to practice at home), clarinet (very hard on the lips) and the cello.
I had always wanted to nurse and was extremely lucky to find a placement at the Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Headington. Then we moved to France where we had a holiday cottage, so I never actually finished the training, but I did attend college in France, learnt the language, and worked for 6 years in a hotel.
I owe my working life experiences to my education received at St Helen’s.”

Partners
Our partnerships embody all the ways we contribute to and learn from the community around us. We build our relationships with local schools and community groups on open dialogue and genuine collaboration, so that inspiration and learning flow in both directions. By giving their time and working alongside others towards a shared goal, our students come to understand the real part they can play in society.
Partnership work is a living, growing part of school life, reaching across the community through many streams: academic, the creative arts, well-being, sport, Futures and charity.
OX14 Learning Partnership
We’re proud to be part of the OX14 Learning Partnership, alongisde Fitzharrys School, John Mason School, Larkmead School, Radley College and Abingdon School. Together, this group of six maintained and independent schools works to raise aspiration across OX14, creating opportunities for students and staff to be challenged, inspired and to learn from one another. It’s a true collaboration, driven by Partnership Champions at every school and by an active OX14 Student Voice Committee, where students and staff shape the venture side by side.
The OX14 Partnership runs a wonderful range of projects. Highlights include:
Peer Support Leads
This programme trains Sixth Form students to become mentors in their schools, sharing good practice across all six. Students of every age gain access to peers who are trained and genuinely passionate about supporting others through any challenge, strengthening the mental health framework of each school. It has proven invaluable for those who seek mentoring, and it’s a powerful leadership opportunity and for those who provide it.
Academic Coaching
Coaching unlocks potential lifts performance through hones, structured conversation. Sixth Form students from across the six schools attend train in the GROW coaching model, which gives shape and direction to a coaching conversation. Older students now coach younger one, and each other, on goals such as beating procrastination, staying calm in exams and working to tight deadlines. In offering that support, the coaches build their own skills of teamwork, communication and listening.
Oxbridge Club
Starting in Year 11, students from across the partnership meet regularly to explore what applying to Oxford and Cambridge really involves. Sessions focus on the critical thinking skills that are so essential for interview, with advice straight from current Oxbridge undergraduate students.
InspirED, ChallengED, SupportED
Each year, the OX14 Partnership runs three flagship core events for Year 8, Year 9 and Year 10 students from all six schools, who work together in cross-school teams with a fresh focus for each one.
Partnership with The Iffley Academy
We are fortunate to work in partnership with The Iffley Academy, a community academy for children and young people up to the age of 18 with complex special educational needs and disabilities. We have an ongoing agreement for reciprocal work experience between the schools this year it’s been a pleasure to host students who were keen to gain experience in grounds maintenance and gardening and there are opportunities for our aspirant veterinary students in their small animal unit.
Other partnerships
Beyond the OX14 Partnership, we take part in a wide range of partnership activities:
Creative partnerships
There are regular opportunities for those who enjoy the creative arts to work with others. We recently hosted an orchestral day in which Oxford Philharmonic led musicians from across the county in activities culminating in a stunning performance. Local primary schools are invited to a matinee performance of the Lower School Production and our Drama Scholars run workshops in these schools to enhance the experience. Our Drama School preparation evening allows students to join with other aspirant actors to learn more about the application process directly from current drama students.
Sports partnerships
Our PE department offers many opportunities which bring together St Helen’s students with students from other local primary and secondary schools from futsal tournaments and introductions to lacrosse to invitational cross-country races, indoor athletics, indoor cricket, netball tournaments and swimming galas.
Community service
Community service is a year-long commitment: a double lesson once a week in the first year of Sixth Form, and it can count towards the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award. It’s a chance for students to work directly with people in the local community, building on the long-standing links St Helen’s has forged with associations and schools across Abingdon. Students may give their time to help at local primary and secondary schools, SEN schools and care homes.

Health Centre and counsellors
Health Centre
Our Health Centre is staffed by our wonderful team of qualified nurses who take the time at the beginning of the school year to get to know each year group and ensure students are aware of the care available to them.
We provide the best possible care to ensure students have the support they need, whether it be suffering from sickness, accident or injury. Students with particular medical needs meet regularly with the school nurses to discuss and review their support.
Our nurses also manage various public health initiatives and vaccination programmes.
Counsellors
Everyone at St Helen’s plays a role in nurturing the mental well-being of our students. We recognise the enormous change that our students undergo as they pass through our school, and the many challenges faced by girls and young women in the 21st century. Sometimes an independent source of help – someone different to a teacher or a friend – is needed to talk through the trickier things.
Our dedicated team of school counsellors provide safe spaces for those needing guidance and care. Counselling sessions are open to all students, who can self-refer or speak to their form tutor, the Pastoral Deputy Head or another trusted staff member to explore what support might be best for them.

Personal development
Personal Development (PD) is an essential part of every student’s week at St Helen’s. It is an opportunity to discuss some of life’s biggest questions as well as everyday challenges that students will face throughout their lives – from friendships and relationships, to issues with mental health, career options, online safety, personal finances, exam preparations, different cultures and much more.
The aim of PD, from SHSK Prep (Junior Department) to Sixth Form, is to encourage students to engage fully in stimulating discussions, develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need to keep themselves healthy and safe, and provide them with crucial tools to help them later in life.
PD is an intrinsic part of the education and pastoral care of our students. Lessons involve a range of activities including roleplay, debate and teamwork that stimulate discussion, provide important information and allow students to reflect and respond in a safe and supported environment. Students develop self-esteem, confidence, independence and a sense of responsibility.
External speakers are used to provide specialist support in areas such as drug education, body image and relationship and sex education. Due diligence is paid to ensure there is a balance in the information provided and that sources are credible.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
The key aim of PD lessons is to allow a safe space for discussion of a range of issues that might affect our SHSK Prep students, allowing them to develop their knowledge of themselves and of the wider world. We work on building resilience and independence, alongside fostering a greater understanding of others.
The programme is designed to be flexible in order to respond to any issues that may arise within the class, the School or the wider world, but always covers the following six key themes through a range of practical and reflective activities:
Family and relationships, including friendship
Health and wellbeing
Diversity and identity
Safety and the changing body
Citizenship
Economic wellbeing
Lower School
Students in Years 7 and 8 have a PD lesson every week which is taught by their form tutor with contributions from other members of staff and outside speakers. The programme is flexible to respond to any issues which might arise in the year group, within the school as a whole or in the wider community.
Year 7
Friendships and teamwork
Transition into secondary school life
Introduction to careers
Relationships and well-being
Health and well-being
Year 8
Communication skills
Relationships and safeguarding
Drug and tobacco education
Financial education
Middle School
Students in Years 9, 10 and 11 have a PD lesson every week which is taught by their form tutor with contributions from other members of staff and outside speakers. The programme is flexible to respond to any issues which might arise in the year group, within the school as a whole or in the wider community.

Wellbeing and personal safety
Digital literacy and online safety
Careers and GCSE choices
Relationships and sex education
Tackling misogyny

Relationships and sex education
Digital literacy – AI

Drugs education
Year 11
Relationships and safeguarding
Exam preparation and A level choices
Digital literacy – financial
Mindfulness and well-being
Sixth Form
Sixth Form students have a timetabled double lesson in which General Studies topics are delivered. A range of external speakers also provide enrichment and thought-provoking discussion.

Relationships and sex education
Global perspectives
Personal safety – drug education, driving
University preparation – UCAS

Governors
Miss Sara Benbow
An Old Girl of St Helen’s, Sara is a barrister and mediator who specialises in resolving property-related disputes. Aside from work and family, she loves all sorts of musical and sporting pursuits, ranging from singing and choral conducting to lacrosse umpiring via bands (French Horn and Alto Sax), rowing and real tennis. A long-suffering fan of West Ham United, Sara brings eternal optimism tempered by life experience to the governing body.
Miss Sara Benbow
Miss Timi Afolami
Timi is a former Old Girl who left St Helen and St Katherine in 2016 to pursue a career in law. After studying Law at the University of Bristol, Timi is now a qualified solicitor at a leading global law firm and her practice focuses on mergers and acquisitions, private equity, equity capital markets and general corporate matters. Timi lives in London and in her spare time enjoys spending time with friends, going to the theatre and attending various live music concerts.
Miss Timi Afolami
Mrs Pauline Cakebread
Pauline’s first career in financial, operational and change management was in global multinational companies such as Unilever, GSK and Dun & Bradstreet, where she progressed to senior leadership roles. She applied the same skills in small independent and venture-backed businesses in a variety of sectors including pharmaceuticals, IT, retail and services, achieving challenging turnaround goals both as Finance and Managing Director. She now runs an independent consulting business.
Mrs Pauline Cakebread
Ms Sharon Cooper
Sharon is currently the Chief Digital Officer at The Economist Group and has been leading technology teams, managing modernisation and digital transformation for over 15 years. Her daughter is an alumna of St Helen and St Katherine. She is a Trustee of a small medical charity and a non-executive director for two other publishing organisations.
Ms Sharon Cooper
Ms Zoe Davies
Zoe is a Strategic HR Business Partner at UK Research and Innovation, with a wealth of experience in staff management and employment matters. Prior to this, she spent many years at St Helen’s as HR Manager until April 2022, developing a strong understanding of school regulatory compliance and the operational realities of an educational environment. She is also a former St Helen’s parent, with both of her daughters thriving during their time at the School, giving her a valuable perspective on the community.
Ms Zoe Davies
Mr David Fawcus
After 17 years as a partner leading the corporate finance team for a Thames Valley chartered accountancy practice, David runs his own corporate and strategy advisory business which he established 12 years ago, providing merger and acquisition services. He is currently the vice-chair of Governors at Pinewood School and has a lead role in their medium- to long-term strategic planning.
Mr David Fawcus
Mrs Jill Hughes
Jill has over 30 years’ experience in strategic marketing, having started her career working in consumer goods for Unilever. She now runs her own consulting business, having previously been Managing Director at Accenture and a board member at Brand Learning. Jill has been a parent at St Helen’s since 2015, and a particularly keen supporter of music and drama events. Jill herself is an enthusiastic performer, performing in “That 70s Choir” at Edinburgh Festival for the last three years.
Mrs Jill Hughes
Miss Kathryn Lea
Kathryn is an Old Girl of St Helen and St Katharine and a chartered accountant who has worked for a global professional services firm since graduating from the University of Southampton with a BSc in Economics. During her career, she has worked across multiple industries providing technology risk consulting advice across a broad range of projects and clients.
Miss Kathryn Lea
Mrs Anne Lynch
A modern and classical linguist, Anne’s career has spanned 32 years in the independent sector as a teacher of French, Deputy Head (Academic) and Principal. Her niece is an alumna of St Helen and St Katharine and her family lives in Abingdon. In addition to her Governorships in the UK, Anne is a trustee of a French educational charity based in the Auvergne. In her spare time, Anne enjoys travel, theatre and is currently learning Welsh.
Mrs Anne Lynch
Mrs Jane MacKay
Jane has a child who attends St Helen and St Katharine. She is a chartered accountant and a tax partner at Crowe U.K. LLP, a national accounting, tax and advisory firm. Through her work, she has a good understanding of tax issues that affect schools as well as charity accounts and SORP reporting. Jane is a passionate advocate for diversity in finance – and generally – and supports girls’ education as one way to achieve this.
Mrs Jane MacKay
Mrs Jenny Mitchell
Jenny is the Advanced Nurse Practitioner, Thoracic Surgery at the John Radcliffe Hospital. Jenny qualified from Queen Margaret, Edinburgh and has over 25 years’ experience in cardiothoracic nursing. One of Jenny’s children is a former student at St Helen’s.
Mrs Jenny Mitchell
Ms Louise Simpson
Louise is the head of a co-educational independent school. Currently in her third headship, she started her headship journey at Bromley High School, working alongside Becky Dougall as she began her headship at Bath. Louise’s career has spanned seven schools, at home and abroad and she has amassed a wealth of experience in the classroom and in school leadership. An environmental scientist, Louise trained as a biology teacher and is passionate about character education.
Ms Louise Simpson
Mrs Berni Stubley
Berni’s teaching career began in Inner London, she worked in three maintained sector schools before moving in 2005 to SHSK as Deputy Head Academic, then Deputy Head from 2011 until retirement in 2021. Berni’s responsibilities beyond academic leadership included SENCO, Investors in People and teacher training. Her daughter enjoyed nine happy years at SHSK. Berni was a governor at Haberdashers Elstree from 2018-2025 where she chaired the Education Committee.

Art and Ceramics
At St Helen and St Katharine, we believe art belongs to everyone – not only future artists, but future thinkers, makers and innovators. In a rapidly changing world, the ability to think visually, work creatively and approach problems with originality is more valuable than ever. Whether students go on to careers in design, technology, media, business or beyond, art equips them with the confidence to shape ideas and the visual world around them.
Our Art Department fosters this mindset, encouraging curiosity, courage and originality. Academic excellence in Art is built on independent learning and expert teaching, ensuring students engage meaningfully with the world around them. Located on the top floor of the School’s original Edwardian building, our well-equipped studios offer a dynamic space for exploration and expression. We also collaborate closely with the Design and Technology (DT) Department, enabling students to push creative boundaries and bring ambitious ideas to life.
We believe art should be inclusive and accessible, which is why our open-call exhibitions welcome all students, regardless of age, experience or whether they formally study art, to showcase their work. This approach fosters a democratic and inspiring artistic community where every student can share their creative voice.
At St Helen and St Katharine, Art is more than a subject, it’s a way of thinking, seeing and preparing for the future.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
The Art and Design Technology curriculum at SHSK Prep offers a thrilling introduction to the world of creativity, where budding artists can develop their skills under the guidance of specialist teachers who help bring their imaginations to life. From the very start, students benefit from expert support, helping them grow in confidence as they experiment with a wide range of materials, techniques and ideas.
The curriculum builds progressively throughout Years 3–6. Lessons in Years 3 and 4 are based in their own Science, Technology, Art and Design room, while Years 5 and 6 use the same specialist facilities as the older students.
Through exploring both two-dimensional and three-dimensional media, students develop a broad artistic skill set, from painting and printmaking to sculpture and textiles. This hands-on approach encourages them to think creatively, experiment boldly and build a strong foundation for future artistic and design exploration.
With specialist teaching and an environment that nurtures curiosity and ambition, Art and Design Technology at SHSK Prep is more than just an introduction to art and design: it is the foundation for a lifelong creative journey.
Lower School
In today’s highly visual world, the ability to create and interpret images is more important than ever. At St Helen and St Katharine, students study both Art and Ceramics, building confidence in both disciplines while learning to produce and understand effective visual communication.
Our curriculum is accessible to all, regardless of experience, with projects that develop skills in both visual and tactile media. We emphasise diverse artistic voices, focusing on female artists and makers to provide a broader perspective beyond the traditional Western canon. By exploring art in context, students learn to think critically and creatively, preparing them to navigate and contribute to an image-driven world.
Middle School
As students progress through Middle School, they can refine their artistic skills and make more independent, creative decisions. In Year 9, they may choose to study Art and/or Ceramics before selecting their GCSE options, where they can pursue Art, Craft and Design or 3D Design. The focus at this stage is on developing a strong visual and tactile vocabulary, enabling students to think beyond prescribed answers and communicate ideas with fluency in an increasingly image-driven world.
To broaden their perspectives, students work with professional visiting artists, gaining insight into the wide range of careers within the creative industries. Practical skills are deepened through hands-on experiences, and all students take part in at least one trip per year, culminating in Year 10 with an inspiring residential visit to Cornwall, a highlight of the course. These experiences encourage students to take creative risks, develop independent thought, and see the wider impact of art beyond the classroom.
Sixth Form
Building on the skills and independence developed in Middle School, our A Level Fine Art course provides students with the freedom and space to refine their personal artistic voice. Many of our Sixth Form students go on to apply for highly competitive degree and foundation courses, not only in the arts, but also in fields such as Maths, Liberal Arts, Engineering, as well as Architecture, Art History and Fine Art. We offer extensive support in developing their portfolios alongside their A Level work, ensuring they are well-prepared for the next step in their diverse career paths.
Sixth Form students benefit from their own studio space, with Upper Sixth students having personal desks, allowing them to work in a focused and inspiring environment. Our well-equipped studios offer a variety of disciplines, including painting, printmaking, life drawing, sculpture, pottery and photography. With access to the studios at lunchtime and every evening, students can continue to work independently, with staff available to offer support and guidance. This flexibility encourages students to think beyond traditional boundaries, refine their visual literacy, and explore how art intersects with the broader world of design, technology and culture.

Biology
Welcome to Biology – where science comes alive! We aim to inspire students to learn about the variety of life on this planet, the complex interactions between species and the intricate detail of the inner workings of cells and organisms. We believe that biology is for everybody, and we hope that our broad and varied curriculum will engage and challenge all students, as well as develop their practical techniques and problem-solving skills.
Our team of experienced teachers are passionate about biology and aim to make lessons fun and exciting for all. We undertake practical work whenever possible, including microscopy, dissection, microbiology, fieldwork, enzyme studies and qualitative testing. All our lessons are taught in our spacious and well-equipped laboratories.
Lower School
Biology in Years 7 and 8 includes lots of hands-on practical activities to introduce the subject and lay its foundations. Lower School Biology is all about having fun! In Years 7 and 8, Biology is taught as part of the science scheme of work by a member of the Science Department.
Year 7 topics include cell structure, human reproduction, plant reproduction, ecology and variation. Time is also spent teaching students how to use several pieces of scientific equipment, particularly microscopes, and students will experience a memorable visit from ‘Animazing’ where they can get up close with a range of exotic animals and learn about their adaptations.
The Year 8 Biology curriculum focuses on human organ systems. Students learn about respiration, gas exchange, the human circulatory system, digestion, the skeleton and microbes. Each class participates in a heart dissection and students carry out practical work involving yeast respiration and microbiology.
Middle School
In Middle School, we start teaching the Edexcel GCSE curriculum in Year 9. Students have a choice between Combined and Separate Science at the start of Year 10.
Middle School students are taught by specialist biology teachers and undertake plenty of practical work to develop their understanding of concepts and practical skills. These include microscopy, dissection, qualitative testing and sampling.

Sixth Form
The OCR A level Biology course contains a wide range of topics, starting with more foundational subject matters such as cell structure and biochemistry and moving on to human anatomy and physiology (the circulatory, respiratory, excretory and nervous systems), ecology (including biodiversity and conservation), more detailed biochemistry (e.g. respiration and photosynthesis), genetics and genetic technology.
The A level qualification is examined by three theory papers at the end of the two-year course and includes questions based on a clear understanding of practical techniques.

Chemistry
Chemistry is the central scientific discipline that equips you with the tools required to understand the world. Its concepts can be applied to a multitude of different fields and the breadth of the subject is vast. From synthesising the most complex drug molecules or analysing trace evidence to solve crimes to developing the next generation of green technologies; chemists find themselves in numerous exciting fields solving the world’s biggest challenges.
Our dedicated teaching staff have a wealth of experience in igniting a passion for chemistry in young minds. The curriculum aims to engage students in chemistry and its applications while providing opportunities to develop critical thinking skills, problem-solving abilities and laboratory techniques. We have four state-of-the-art chemistry laboratories and, with the help of our highly qualified chemistry technician, regular experimental work across the age range ensures learners become confident practical chemists. As well as preparing students for further scientific study, we aim to instil an awareness of the impact of chemical sciences on our lives, our environment and our society, and enable learners to leave school as true global citizens.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
At St Helen’s, we believe that studying science helps students appreciate and understand the rapidly changing and evolving world in which they live. We foster curiosity and give students the skills to explore their ideas and questions.
The core of our science programme is the National Curriculum, with opportunities for extension built in, including plenty of practical work.
Years 3 and 4 are based in their own Science, Technology, Art and Design classroom, and practicals include investigating the effect of friction on toy cars and the impact of different variables on plant growth.
In Years 5 and 6, students progress to learning in their own fully equipped laboratory in the Science Centre. They enjoy practical experiments, including using Bunsen burners to explore reversible and irreversible changes of states.
With an engaging curriculum and access to the exceptional facilities and resources of the senior school, we are committed to making learning hands-on, ambitious, rewarding and fun. We are not only inspiring young minds but also providing them with the skills required to thrive in Year 7.
Lower School
Year 7 students learn fundamentals such as states of matter, atoms, elements, and the periodic table. They then go on to discover acids and alkalis, chemical reactions and separating mixtures through investigative work. They explore the three sciences on a rotation system throughout the academic year. In Year 8, students move on to study further chemical reactions, including those of metals and fuels. Writing chemical equations helps develop an understanding of these reactions, while a foray into environmental science gives learners an appreciation of how chemistry can help us understand our world. A specialist teacher will guide them through a variety of experiments and demonstrations designed to build on their knowledge and skills from Year 7.
Middle School
In Year 9, students embark upon the academically rigorous Edexcel GCSE Chemistry qualification, which strikes a balance between traditional and contemporary chemistry. Learners are encouraged to be curious about the world around them as well as to think critically. GCSE Chemistry is taught by subject experts in our dedicated laboratories. Our enthusiastic teachers aim to foster an awareness not only of the vast range of applications of chemistry but also the economic, ethical and societal implications of the subject. From Year 10, students can elect to study three separate sciences or combined sciences; both qualifications are the beginning of an exciting journey of discovery, which could lead to further study at A level and beyond.
Sixth Form
Whether you are considering a future in a science-based or medical field, or simply because you love the subject, A level Chemistry builds on GCSE understanding and provides a foundation for higher-level study. The OCR Chemistry A course covers key concepts of chemistry and practical skills are integrated throughout. The combination of academic challenge and practical focus ensures Chemistry is a popular Sixth Form option.

English
English language and literature are at the heart of the way our students see and understand the world around them. We introduce students to a range of texts, authors and ideas to challenge and stimulate debate. As they develop their appreciation of the subtleties of language and literature, our students develop the most effective communication in their everyday lives, from improving their connections with their friends to critiquing the words of politicians.
Around a core of classic and modern literature, the diversity of our curriculum is the product of the scope of personal interests of our passionate and experienced teaching team – from world myths, social linguistics, metaphysical poetry and women’s middlebrow fiction, to sci-fi, graphic novels and Medieval verse. Students are encouraged to join us in developing their own unique literary journey and to share that with each other.
SHSK Prep (Junior Department)
Our English curriculum develops confident and capable communicators, who read widely, write with purpose and speak thoughtfully. We provide frequent oracy opportunities in our lessons and are keen for students to find their voice and ask questions to further their understanding of the world.
During their time in SHSK Prep, students will work with a range of fiction, non-fiction and poetry texts, which will help extend their comprehension and text-analysis skills, as well as inspire their writing. They will practise creating their own texts, while across Prep they will also encounter a range of writing styles, including creative writing, non-chronological reports, newspaper articles and persuasive writing.
We foster a love of reading for pleasure and make weekly visits to our extensive school library. We encourage students and staff to give book recommendations, and have excellent librarians who have deep and wide-ranging knowledge of children’s literature.
We aim for a balance between encouraging creativity in writing and ensuring our students have the fundamental technical skills needed to become proficient readers and writers. We therefore plan frequent opportunities to work on reading, handwriting, spelling, punctuation and grammar skills.
By Year 6, students will have the confidence to bring together all of their skills and knowledge in their Young Entrepreneur project. During this project, they will work on their formal presentation skills and persuasive writing.
Lower School
Our Year 7 and Year 8 curriculum encourages creativity and diversity: eco-dystopia, feminist historical drama, identity politics in Shakespeare and our independent reading project of literary voices from around the world, which culminates in a virtual exhibition of artefacts responding to six different contemporary novels. We add new novels from the Carnegie list to classroom study each year, making text decisions in collaboration with students in response to their reading interests. We study verse novels, such as The Crossing and Clap When You Land, next to descriptive writing about dinosaurs, Romantic poetry and our annual debating contest, as well as a lively Shakespeare By Heart competition. We embrace the freedom that these two years of English study offer to students and give dedicated library time to quiet reading, book review games and literary quizzes.
Middle School
Middle School prepares students for GCSEs in both English Language and English Literature. We study An Inspector Calls as our modern text, a play that has found renewed resonance with students in issues around labour strikes, the cost-of-living crisis, generational divides and sexism in the #MeToo era. In Macbeth, students explore ever-relevant ideas about power and politics, and Pride and Prejudice offers an appreciation for satire and vibrant discussions around modern gender roles and relationships. We study a range of poems, alongside an inspiring focus on creative writing, and a range of non-fiction that includes our speechwriting competition, from which a number of students go on to compete in inter-school public speaking events. At the heart of all our study is the development of analytical skills that allow students to access texts independently at GCSE and beyond.
Sixth Form
A level English Literature ranges over 600 years of writing – from Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales in the 14th century to Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie’s Americanah and Sally Rooney’s Normal People in the 21st century. Students learn how to construct complex arguments, developing the skill of effective written communication that will stay with them for life. The empathy gained from literary study is well-documented and is at the heart of classroom discussions.
The A level process asks students to narrow their focus to just a few subjects, but by choosing English they instead broaden their scope to everything that literature embraces: psychology, philosophy, history, linguistics, anthropology, politics and more. To choose to study English Literature at A level is to choose to study the whole world that we all live in.

Our popular Literary Societies extend students’ experiences of literature and language. We explore all and everything – comics, Old English, crime novels, linguistics – and students learn to undertake their own literary research projects. On our A level Literary Retreat to London, we take in theatrical shows (ideally one at the Globe and one more contemporary performance at a theatre such as the National or the Bridge), develop our creative writing in response to the Treasures section of the British Library, and enjoy a literary walking tour around Bloomsbury with actors performing poetry and scenes from writers’ lives.

Careers
The work within the Careers Department reflects a whole school ethos and mission to inspire and champion excellence for all students in whatever career path they choose.
At St Helen’s we understand that students can feel daunted about the future. With the wide variety of paths and possibilities open to them, making decisions about their future in an uncertain world, plus understanding what aspects are truly important to them, can potentially feel like an emotional rollercoaster!
We therefore see it as crucial that students begin learning about careers and the world of work from Year 5 and continue all the way through to Upper Sixth. This ensures that every student leaves school with a good awareness of the emerging and differing opportunities and career paths alongside traditional professional routes. They also have the self-knowledge, skills, and resilience to thrive in society as a successful young adult; maximising their individual strengths, talents and potential.
Whether it’s the Young Entrepreneur project in Year 6, the action packed ‘Business Brains and Entrepreneurship’ day in Year 8, the day’s work shadowing as part of ‘World of Work Day’ in Year 9, the two weeks’ work experience in Year 11 or listening to one of the fascinating talks by visiting speakers, students have so many opportunities to immerse themselves in discovering more about the world of work. This in turn enables every student to feel supported, confident and well-informed to fulfil their potential and meet their aspirations. Our open-door policy encourages students from across all year groups to either pop in or make an appointment to talk to the careers team who are available every day.
Career Development Institute
St Helen’s is also proud to be a long-term member of the Career Development Institute and have received an excellence award from Investors in Careers.
We are also immensely proud of our wonderful, purpose-built careers library. It is open to all students across the whole school and is kept up-to-date with the latest careers books and reference material in both printed and digital format. Students are also provided with logins to a useful array of online career packages. This enables students to individually research information on different occupations, apprenticeships, universities, gap years, the labour market, career pathways and UCAS applications.
Working together
Thanks to links with alumnae, parents, other schools in the Oxfordshire area, local and national employers and organisations, the careers provision is greatly enhanced and ensures that students’ learning is current and relevant. This involvement boosts the provision of work experience placements, curriculum projects, careers talks and the annual careers convention. The Careers Department is always aiming to expand links and if you are interested in volunteering some of your time, experience and expertise to support an event or activity, please get in touch with Mrs Emily Cartwright, Head of Careers and Professional Guidance.
We are enormously proud of our alumnae whose remarkable achievements and sphere of influence are evident in every walk of life, from medicine, business and engineering to law, public policy and the arts. We are extremely fortunate that so many stay in contact and generously give their time, expertise, skills and professional advice to current Sixth Form students through the Kate Scheme, our career mentoring programme. The aim is to inspire and guide students as they make the transition between school, higher education and first career. This initial step to a professional network brings lifelong advantage.
The Careers Programme
Our careers provision takes into consideration the Gatsby benchmarks plus the Career Development Framework developed by the Career Development Institute. The current careers programme is delivered through careers lessons provided within the Personal Development (PD) programme from Years 5 through to Sixth Form.

Futures – HE and careers
Futures at St Helen’s is about encouraging you to lift your gaze above A levels in order to inspire, challenge and prepare you for life after school. Higher education, careers and alumnae support blend seamlessly to elevate our students’ aspirations, giving you access to specialist university experts, career guidance consultants and alumnae who are making waves in every field imaginable, and who are keen to connect with you and encourage you to go for it, whatever ‘it’ may be.
Higher education
The majority of our students go on to higher education from school or after a gap year. We ensure that you find the transition as smooth as possible by providing university-style experiences both in and out of the classroom – by the end of your time at St Helen’s, you will be well aware of the academic workload, expectations and pace expected at university.
You will have the opportunity to explore the many avenues available, and our Sixth Form and Careers teams, as well as tutors and subject specialists, will support and guide you through application processes for your chosen path. An evening of talks from higher education experts takes place in Lower Sixth, as well as an annual partnership event alternately focusing on medicine and veterinary medicine applications, and Oxbridge entry. Or, if you are thinking about studying abroad, our international university fair and one-to-one guidance will open up horizons and offer advice.
Our support extends from the beginning of your time at St Helen’s into your time at university – our ‘UniversiTea’ scheme helps connect students who are starting university with St Helen’s alumnae already there, offering you a friendly face to meet up with in a new place.
Higher education programme
The Higher education team provides a full programme of information, advice and guidance to support each student in their choices and to help them to make an informed decision for their future education and career. The work within the Careers and Higher Education Departments reflects a whole school ethos and mission to inspire and champion excellence for all of the students in the career path they choose. Central to the work is developing awareness of emerging and differing opportunities and career paths, alongside traditional routes, to maximise each student’s individual strengths, talents and potential.

Your long-term ambitions are a key area of focus during your time at St Helen’s. You will work with members of Futures Team to expand your experience, understanding and knowledge in order to give you the best possible foundation for pursuing those ambitions.
Several careers events take place throughout the academic year. Our annual joint Careers Convention with other local schools brings together a huge array of career representatives from medicine and architecture to the financial industry and aerospace engineering.
The Kate Scheme offers a full range of mentoring and formal advice opportunities to students. Our alumnae offer their skills and advice to help you pursue professional opportunities through encouragement, sharing experiences and instilling confidence. The aim is to inspire and guide you as you make the transition between school, higher education and your career. This first step to a professional network brings lifelong advantage.
We are enormously proud of our alumnae whose remarkable achievements and sphere of influence are evident in every walk of life, from medicine, business and engineering to law, public policy and the arts. We are extremely fortunate that so many stay in regular contact and generously give their time and expertise to current students and each other.

Policies and inspection reports
Inspection Reports
Inspection report 2025
ISI school inspection March 2025
An Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection under Framework 23 took place in March 2025. We are delighted that St Helen and St Katharine was found to be fully compliant with all Independent School Standards and particularly proud that our co-curricular provision was identified as a ‘Significant Strength’ of the School. We are also very pleased that the report describes our curriculum as “suitably academic and demanding, reflecting the needs and abilities of pupils”, and that the inspectors found that “many activities [are designed] to support pupils’ emotional and mental well-being as a balance to the focus of the academic curriculum”.
Inspection report 2022
ISI focused compliance and educational quality inspection February 2022
An Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection took place in February 2022 and was a focused compliance and educational quality inspection. We were delighted that we met all of the regulatory elements of the focussed compliance inspection, and were graded as ‘Excellent’ for both the students’ academic and personal development. The focus of all inspections is upon the outcomes for students, and we were particularly thrilled by the positive responses of students and parents in the pre-inspection questionnaires.
Inspection report 2017
ISI regulatory compliance inspection October 2017
An Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) compliance inspection took place in October 2017. A compliance inspection focuses on the safety and well-being of students and staff, and we were delighted to have met all regulatory requirements and had no follow-up actions or recommendations. We were also delighted by the positive feedback from our parent body and students in the pre-inspection questionnaires; the level of response was described as 'extraordinary' by the Reporting Inspector.
